passage: It was past bedtime, and Farhan, two, sat cross-legged on the bed rocking back and forth, one hand on his blanket, eyes half closed. He had cried when the lights went off, and now his rocking slowed to a gentle sway. Ganga sat in the chair by the door and watched. She did not stop him. She hummed the tune he liked and kept her voice low. After a little while the swaying stopped, his head tipped sideways onto the pillow and his breath deepened.

qa.q: What was Farhan doing on the bed?
qa.a: Rocking back and forth cross-legged with one hand on his blanket.

qa.q: What do you think Farhan's rocking helped him feel?
qa.a: It seemed to help him settle after the upset of the lights going off, as his rocking slowed into sleep. It could also just be a habit that comforts him.

qa.q: What could Ganga do if the rocking ever seemed to worry her?
qa.a: She could mention it to the doctor, especially if it goes on a lot or Farhan seems cut off from her.

qa.q: How might Farhan feel with Ganga nearby?
qa.a: He may feel safe because someone he loves is close and humming.

grounding: A toddler rocks and sways to calm down and fall asleep, a common way to settle strong feelings.

passage:
“Yogesh, come up here,” said Swati, patting her knee. Yogesh climbed on, still sniffling after a loud thunderclap.
“That was noisy.”
He began to bounce on her knee, small bounces, in time with his breath.
“You bounce it out?”
He nodded, and bounced.
“I'm here.”
The bouncing became slower and slower.
“Better?”
“Bet-ter,” said Yogesh, leaning back against her chest with his thumb in his mouth.

qa.q: What frightened Yogesh?
qa.a: A loud thunderclap.

qa.q: What do Yogesh's small bounces on her knee show he was doing?
qa.a: He was calming himself after the fright, as the bouncing slowed and he said “Better”. It might also be a comfort habit he likes.

qa.q: What could Swati do next time there is thunder?
qa.a: She could hold him early, keep her voice soft and let him bounce until he is ready to stop.

qa.q: How might Yogesh see Swati's knee?
qa.a: It is probably a safe, warm place where he can rock himself back to calm.

grounding: A toddler bounces on a knee to calm down after a fright, a common way of settling strong feelings.

passage: Daycare note, Friday. After her mother left, Gurpreet sat on the mat and rocked forward and back, humming, for a few minutes. She still looked up when I spoke and took my hand when I offered it. At nap time she rocked again, slower, until she fell asleep. This looks like her way of calming down. I have shared it with her parents; if the rocking ever seems distressing, or she stops responding to us, they can mention it to the paediatrician. Saurabh, daycare teacher

qa.q: What did Gurpreet do after her mother left?
qa.a: She sat on the mat and rocked forward and back, humming.

qa.q: What might Gurpreet's rocking mean about how she was feeling?
qa.a: It likely shows she was sad or unsettled after her mother left and was calming herself; she still looked up and took Saurabh's hand, so she stayed connected.

qa.q: What would you advise Gurpreet's parents?
qa.a: Treat the rocking as a normal way she soothes herself, and mention it to the paediatrician if it ever seems distressing or she stops responding.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: They might feel a little worried at first, then reassured by the detail that she stayed in contact and settled.

grounding: A teacher sees a toddler rock to calm herself after a goodbye and at nap time, noting what would be worth raising with a paediatrician.

passage:
Irawati tripped on the bamboo step of their village house and sat down hard. She didn't cry loudly. She sat with her knees up, swaying side to side, humming a tuneless note.
Lalremsiami, her grandmother, put down the rice she was cleaning and sat near her, not touching yet. She began to sway too, humming the same note. After a while Irawati leaned against her and the swaying slowed and stopped.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami doing before Irawati tripped?
qa.a: She was cleaning rice.

qa.q: What was Irawati feeling as she swayed and hummed?
qa.a: She was likely shaken and upset after the fall and was calming herself; leaning on her grandmother shows she then wanted comfort.

qa.q: Which choice of Lalremsiami's worked, and why?
qa.a: Sitting near and swaying with her, without rushing to touch, worked because it joined Irawati's own way of settling.

qa.q: How might it feel for Lalremsiami when Irawati leans against her?
qa.a: She would likely feel tender and glad that Irawati trusted her enough to lean in.

grounding: A toddler sways and hums to calm herself after a fall, and her grandmother joins in until she settles.

passage:
The family dinner in Amman was loud with cousins and clattering plates. Rania climbed onto Siddiq's knee and began bouncing herself, up and down, eyes half closed.
"She wants a game," said an aunt.
Siddiq shook his head. "She's settling." He bounced his knee gently to her rhythm. Slowly Rania's bounces got smaller, her head tipped onto his chest, and she was asleep before the dessert came.

qa.q: Whose knee did Rania climb onto?
qa.a: Siddiq's knee.

qa.q: What was Rania likely feeling as she bounced with her eyes half closed?
qa.a: She was likely tired and overwhelmed by the noisy dinner and was bouncing to calm herself toward sleep.

qa.q: What did Siddiq do that helped Rania?
qa.a: He matched her rhythm gently instead of turning it into a lively game, so she could settle and sleep.

qa.q: Why might the aunt read the bouncing differently from Siddiq?
qa.a: The aunt sees a child bouncing and assumes play, while Siddiq notices her half-closed eyes and the noise around her.

grounding: A toddler bounces on her father's knee to settle in a noisy room, and he reads it as self-soothing.

passage:
I'm Sarika, from the flat opposite. Some evenings I sit with Lokesh's mother while she gets him to sleep.
He sits on her lap and rocks, forward, back, forward, back, while she hums. Sometimes he sways side to side with his eyes half closed. His fists open. Then he's asleep.
I asked if the rocking was normal. She said it seems to settle him, and if it ever looked like it upset him, she'd mention it to the doctor.

qa.q: What does Lokesh's mother do while he rocks?
qa.a: She hums while he rocks.

qa.q: What does Lokesh's rocking seem to do for him at bedtime?
qa.a: It seems to help him calm down and feel settled enough to sleep, shown by his fists opening and eyes half closing.

qa.q: What is sensible about his mother's view of the rocking?
qa.a: She lets him use it to settle, while planning to mention it to the doctor if it ever seemed to upset him.

qa.q: How does Sarika see the rocking at first?
qa.a: Sarika was unsure and a little curious, and asked whether it was normal.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler rocking and swaying to settle for sleep, with a parent ready to mention it to a doctor if it ever seemed distressing.
